featured_reviews.review_text:
The south Indian food here is a must have if you're visiting this place. So this was my go to spot for all the times I've gone for cycling to Versova beach. The best part about this restaurant is that it opens up really early in the morning so fortunately I can have a wholesome breakfast and continue with my cycling. I've tried their Medu Vada, idli, sabudana Vada, neer dosa, onion rava dosa and I've loved all of them except for the sabudana Vada which wasn't cooked well from inside. But overall a really good place to try out.

Edit: 11-Oct-2024
my recent visit to this hotel has made me change my mind, especially when the staff picked up the rasgolas that were fallen on the floor and packed them back in the containers that would be sent to the customers.

I seen them coating the rasgulas with the special floor coat and then packing them in lovely boxes.

made me wonder, may be that's where the rasgolas got their shine from and also maybe the taste as it was a more earthly flavour and boot smelling taste.

I had ordered my regular medu wada sambar and lassi, but after looking at the hygiene that they displayed, made me wonder what was in my food???

Will definitely visit again!

featured_reviews.name: Vaibhav Bhosale
featured_reviews.review_text:
Tanjore Tiffin Room, Versova – Authentic South Indian Delight!

Visited **Tanjore Tiffin Room, Versova** on Sunday with a group of 12, and the experience was fantastic!

The **Chicken Ghee Roast, Chicken Chintamani, and Pepper Chicken** were absolutely outstanding - rich, spicy, and packed with authentic South Indian flavors. 🍗🔥
We also loved the **Malabar Parotta, Appam, Idiyappam, and Dosa with Sambar** - soft, fresh, and perfect with the curries.

Veg dishes like **Jackfruit Cutlet and Jackfruit Biryani** were surprisingly delicious, and the **Chicken Biryani** was aromatic and generously portioned. The **Mango Mint Cooler** was a refreshing highlight after the spicy feast. 🥭❄️

If the main seating area is full, they have **additional seating inside WTF**, which is very convenient during peak hours.
They also offer a **tasting platter where the staff explains different curries and how they are used in cooking** - a brilliant concept for first-time visitors and food enthusiasts.

The restaurant is **just ~500 meters from Versova Metro Station**, making it very easy to reach. 🚇

For around **₹9.7K for 12 people (~₹800 per person)**, the quality, quantity, and taste were totally worth it.

**Highly recommended for authentic South Indian food and group outings! Will definitely visit again.**

featured_reviews.name: shripad marathe
featured_reviews.review_text:
Finally got to visit Amritsr in Andheri West after hearing so much about their Thailand and Dubai outlets, and it absolutely lived up to the hype! This place is a paradise for anyone who loves authentic Punjabi cuisine.

The Food:
Every dish we tried was bursting with authentic flavors. The Keema Kulcha Mutton with Chicken Gravy was phenomenal – perfectly spiced and incredibly tender. The Amritsari Mix Kulcha with Chholle was a classic done right, with the kulchas being soft, buttery, and generously stuffed.

The Bhalla Papdi Chaat from their live chaat counter was fresh and delicious. For non-veg lovers, the Chicken Seekh Kebab, Rawas Ajwain Fish Tikka, and especially the Prawns Fry Koliwada (their Bombay Special) were absolute showstoppers. The Butter Chicken and Mutton Barrah Masala were rich, flavorful, and cooked to perfection.

The Drinks:
Their cocktail menu is creative and fun! We tried the Jamun-Tini, Kulangan Elixer, Achari Whiskey, and White on the Top – each one was unique and well-crafted. The authentic lassi is a must-try and pairs beautifully with the spicy food.

The Experience:
The ambiance screams fine dining with warm Punjabi hospitality. The live chaat counters add an interactive element, and the service was attentive without being intrusive. Don't miss the 'Wishing Well' – a fun concept where you could win discounts or even get your entire meal free!

Final Verdict:
If you're craving authentic Punjabi food with a fine dining twist, Amritsr is the place to be. Already planning our next visit!

Highly recommended! 💯

featured_reviews.name: Purple R
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Project Hum on a Tuesday for lunch.

We had the Rad Thai Chicken and Lean Chicken with 2 sides. Both were delicious and promptly cooked. The Matcha Mango was refreshing, as was the Lemonella.

One small observation: a few menu items were unavailable during our visit. When I asked about one of them, I was told the restaurant had been closed on Monday and some items were not yet prepared. It wasn't an issue for us as we enjoyed what we ordered, but it may be worth keeping in mind if you're visiting early in the week.

My only real criticism is the service charge. The ordering system is self-service: you order and pay at the counter, and the cashier simply takes payment and hands over the bill. That's perfectly fine, but I was confused as to why a service charge was added. It also feels a little awkward to question it AFTER PAYMENT has already been made.

I've been to places with similar systems, such as Suzette, where no service charge is applied. If this were a sit-down, table-service experience, I wouldn't mind. Alternatively, if the charge is clearly disclosed on the menu, that would help (unless I happened to miss it).

Overall, a great meal and I'd happily return. The service charge policy is the only reason for the 4/5 rating.

featured_reviews.name: Swapnil Chavan
featured_reviews.review_text: A masterclass in texture and spice, the Chole Samosa Chaat here is a sensory riot where the shattered, golden crunch of the samosa is beautifully surrendered to a deep, tangy chickpea curry, all elevated by a cooling drizzle of yogurt and the electric snap of fresh chutneys. To recreate this at home, simmer boiled chickpeas in a masala of onions, ginger-garlic, and amchoor, then ladle it over crushed hot samosas and finish with a snowfall of fine sev and chopped onions. In a sophisticated contrast, the Rava Dosa arrives as a shatteringly crisp, lacy veil of gold; its secret lies in a buttermilk-thin batter of semolina, rice flour, and cumin poured from a height onto a screaming-hot griddle until it develops its signature "Swiss-cheese" holes. Whether you’re diving into the indulgent, street-style chaos of the chaat or the ethereal, buttery crispness of the dosa, this is a dual-course experience that perfectly celebrates the diverse landscape of Indian soul food.

Visited Cream Centre recently, mainly because it’s a pure vegetarian spot and we had heard quite a bit about it. We tried the American corn cheese balls, chilli wontons in spicy sauce, Chaat platter, and their famous “World’s Best” loaded nachos. Overall, the food was decent—nothing extraordinary, but not disappointing either. The standout for us was definitely the nachos, which actually lived up to the hype.

What did disappoint us though was the sizzler menu. Cream Centre is quite popular for its sizzlers, and we were really looking forward to trying them. Unfortunately, out of eight options, only two were available at the time, which was a bit of a letdown.

As for the ambience and service(thanks to Gayatri), both were just okay—nothing to complain about, but nothing particularly memorable either.

Overall, a decent place for vegetarian food, but it didn’t quite match the expectations we had going in.

featured_reviews.name: GLEN MONTEIRO
featured_reviews.review_text:
Loco Loca is a cordial, lively place located on the ground floor of The Empresa Hotel. The ambiance of this place is characterized by its open air kitchen and it's enticing canopy. The Spanish and Italian folk music playing in the background incites feelings of cravings and euphoria. The place is embellished with an amazing set up in the dining area with spacious seating. On top of that, the dessert bar with an amazing line up of sweet treats and confectionery adds to the charm.

The bistro makes you feel in your element with their camaraderie. The atmosphere of this place and the crew connive to make the customer feel like a huésped as they embrace them to their ménage.

The service was pretty good. Our table was hosted by Mr. Rahul, Mr. Nikhil and Mr. Vishal. They helped us out in selecting the dishes and were very friendly. The restaurant being an part of The Empresa, has to manage the hotel guests along with the adventurous diners who visit the place. So it may take a while to get what you order but the food is totally worth the wait.

They serve a variety of dishes from the Mediterranean and North Indian Cuisine. The menu is pretty elaborate and covers a lot of palatable dishes with top class presentation. The chefs collude to serve appetizing and innovative dishes to appease the diners and bring a smile of satisfaction on their faces.

Our table was festooned with salads, burgers, appetizers, risotto and desserts.
We started off with 'Feta & Co. '. It's a salad constructed with the Greek Feta and a combination of fresh fruits and mixed greens. The salty and tangy taste of Feta combined with the flavours of fresh fruits and avocado makes it one of the finest salads in the menu.

The 'Supreme Crisp Burger' had the perfect cohesiveness between the amount of bun, meat and toppings. It was a merger of the chicken supreme patty, onion rings with the side of potato wedges. The bun was nicely toasted to hold up the patty. The quality of the meat used was top class which made the burger very juicy.
We also had 'Easy green Burger' which was served with a side of potato wedges and salads. It had a delectable taste.

Mediterranean food is more than just pizza and spaghetti, for a change, we ordered 'Grilled Portobello & Asparagus Risotto'. It was ambrosial! Amazing taste. The 'Potato Mille-Feuille' was very appetizing. The combination of fried potatoes and wild mushrooms with parmesan ragoût made it delicious!

We had a few beverages here: 'Passion Fruit Chilli Lemonade' and 'Blueberry & Basil lemonade'. They were very refreshing. The passion fruit chilli tasted really good. It had a spicy twist to it.

They serve some of the most bewitching and delicious desserts. We had 'Hazelnut Mousse' and 'Chocolate Chip Cupcake'. The Hazelnut mousse is one the best desserts I've had in a while. It tasted heavenly with a the base made of chocolate crumbs. The cup cake tasted alright. I liked the Mousse more.

Mediterranean food is one of those cultural elements that have felicitously helped to preserve the special nature of the Mediterranean.
When it comes to Mediterranean Cuine, Loco loca is definitely one of the best places in town.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Serious Food Safety Issue & Request for Accountability

We visited Persian Darbar expecting a good dining experience; however, it resulted in a serious health issue.

We ordered a combination of vegetarian and non-vegetarian dishes. From the vegetarian items, Paneer Tikka Masala was partially left, packed, and taken home. The next day, all five of us who consumed the food suffered from loose motion, fever, and vomiting. Subsequently, our parents also consumed the same packed food and experienced identical symptoms.

This strongly points toward poor food quality or lack of freshness. Due to this incident:
•	Multiple family members required medical attention
•	We incurred doctor consultation and medication expenses
•	I missed work, and my parents also lost working days
•	We faced significant physical discomfort and mental stress

Dining at a reputed restaurant should create good memories—not lead to health trauma and medical emergencies.

Given the seriousness of this incident, we believe the management should take responsibility and compensate us for the medical expenses, lost workdays, and the distress caused. At the very least, we expect acknowledgment of the issue and assurance of corrective measures to prevent this from happening to other customers.

This review is shared in the interest of consumer awareness and accountability.

featured_reviews.name: Dr Prasad Kamble
featured_reviews.review_text:
Banana Leaf is a great place for anyone who loves authentic vegetarian South Indian food. We tried a few of their delicacies—filter coffee, appam, and the Benne Podi Masala Dosa.
My absolute favorite was the Benne Podi Masala Dosa. It’s not like the traditional benne dosa that comes drenched in coconut oil—this version is neat, easy to eat, and definitely feels healthier. It’s served with white butter (makkhan), flavorful chutney, and sambar, which perfectly balance the dosa.
The filter coffee was comforting and well brewed, and the appam was soft and light. They have a wide range of South Indian delicacies on the menu, and there’s a lot more I’m looking forward to trying.
I’ll definitely keep updating my reviews as and when we visit again. For now, the Benne Podi Masala Dosa is completely on my mind and a must-try! 😋

The misal had a good balance of spice, the batata vada was crisp, and the puri bhaji was satisfying and filling. The ambience is simple and clean, with a calm, no-frills setup that suits a traditional vegetarian restaurant. It has a homely, comfortable feel, making it ideal for families and casual dining. The seating is basic but well maintained, and the overall atmosphere is peaceful and welcoming, letting the food remain the main highlight.

Overall, a good place for a wholesome vegetarian meal.

featured_reviews.name: Yati Soni
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re craving authentic, no-frills South Indian food in Juhu, Sri Annapoorna Cafe is an absolute gem. The menu is refreshingly simple, but every item delivers on taste, quality, and authenticity.

The sambhar is rich, perfectly spiced, and feels like it’s straight out of a traditional South Indian kitchen. The benne podi masala dosa is a standout—crispy on the outside, generously layered with butter, and packed with flavorful podi that hits just right.

The idli with rasam is comfort in a plate—soft, fluffy idlis paired with a tangy, soul-warming rasam that you’ll want to keep sipping. And the vada? Crisp on the outside, soft inside, and absolutely worth the hype.

What really sets this place apart is how it sticks to its roots—no unnecessary gimmicks, just honest, traditional flavors done right. Add to that the pocket-friendly pricing, and you’ve got a spot that’s truly worth every rupee.

Simple menu, authentic taste, and consistently good food—definitely a must-visit for South Indian lovers.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Thank you for the wonderful 5-star rating and for taking the time to share such a detailed experience.
We’re truly delighted to know that you enjoyed the Benne Podi Masala Dosa, idli with rasam, vada, and our sambar. It means a lot to us that you appreciated the authenticity, flavors, and the effort we put into maintaining traditional South Indian taste.
Your words about our simple menu, consistency, and no-frills approach are especially encouraging, as that is exactly what we aim to deliver—honest food made with care and quality ingredients.
We’re also glad you found the experience value for money and worthy of recommendation. Feedback like yours motivates our entire team to continue maintaining these standards every single day.
Thank you once again for your kind support. We look forward to welcoming you back to Sri Annapoorna Cafe.

Filter coffee is the only thing that was good.
Was shocked with the quality considering such good reviews.

During busy hours, our team may cross-check payments to avoid any confusion, and there is never an intention to make a guest uncomfortable.
We understand taste can be subjective and appreciate you bringing this to our attention.
